result:
If I could change the world in one way, I would make universal, high-quality education the lived reality for every child and adult—education that emphasizes critical thinking, scientific literacy, emotional intelligence, and empathy.

That single change would shift so many downstream problems: better public reasoning and less susceptibility to misinformation, more cooperation across difference, improved health and economic opportunity, and a broader pool of people capable of solving complex challenges like climate change and public-health crises. Teaching people how to learn and how to think together creates durable capacities rather than temporary fixes.

It’s not the only change the world needs, but giving everyone the tools to understand problems, evaluate evidence, and care for one another would multiply the impact of every other improvement.
